tier2.text: A Merkel cell is a touch-sensing cell in the epidermis, the outermost layer of the skin. Merkel cells stimulate sensory nerves, and the brain perceives these nerve signals as touch. Merkel cells are mechanoreceptors, receptors for physical stimuli such as pressure and vibration. When a finger drags across a textured surface, the skin vibrates, and Merkel cells sense these low-frequency vibrations. Merkel cells lie in the stratum basale, the deepest layer of the epidermis. There, Merkel cells are scattered among basal cells, stem cells that keep dividing to make new cells of the epidermis. Merkel cells are especially abundant on the surfaces of the hands and feet.
